verdict.rationale: Navan documents a public API covering the expense surface: OAuth client credentials, retrieve/update endpoints for card transactions, manual expenses, repayments, disputes and similar records, custom-field management, receipts and webhooks. It also offers an official MCP server, but that server is described mainly as a way to query spend, policy and card data. Nothing shows the API reaching parity with the UI: travel booking and changes, policy and approval-workflow configuration, rewards and reimbursements appear only as product or UI features, and the MCP is framed as read and query access rather than full actions. missing for 10: API coverage for travel booking/changes/cancellations, policy and approval workflow management via API, an explicit UI-parity statement, write/action capabilities through MCP, independent corroboration of API breadth.
